issue_request: FHIR-22763 was a Published/Persuasive Financial Management issue asking to remove dummy ICD-10 concepts from Claim valueset-icd-10 and fix related examples to use valid ICD-10 or ICD-10-CM codes.
initial_application: Jira comments cite pre-applied commits b55203191d0acf262425888825ef4f77a11e4841, 820b4fa08422d7d405c5cea644b7a659af307086, and 24bf09a6ea30590a77c65da3ccd04a389ad53a58. Those commits commented out invalid dummy ValueSet concepts, updated Claim examples to ICD-10-CM where appropriate, replaced the oral orthodontic dummy code with K07.3, fixed a historical ChargeItem example, and corrected ServiceRequest/example display details.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Claim and ServiceRequest as active current-build resources; ChargeItem is not an active current-build resource. The current Claim ICD-10 ValueSet includes the ICD-10 system without active dummy concepts, and current relevant examples use M96.1, G89.4, M53.88, M47.816, K07.3, and E84.0. The 2019 committers Zulip thread confirms the original build failure came from dummy ICD-10 codes and that Rob Hausam cleaned it up. No Confluence reference or conflicting community evidence was found.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current core source already preserves the applied resolution and no further in-scope source edit is needed.
